items.title: 102 Avenue Bike Route (111-136 Street) Fact Sheet
items.source_date: 2017; exact publication and last-updated dates not stated in the document

citations.finding: The City's 2017 102 Avenue fact sheet says the segment from 121 Street to 111 Street was a two-way roadway and would be converted to one-way eastbound, with a protected bike lane proposed. This supports a qualifying lane conversion on the named segment, though it does not establish the full census or geographic threshold.
citations.establishes: The City described the 121 Street to 111 Street segment as two-way before the project and planned to convert it to one-way eastbound while adding a protected bike lane.

citations.finding: For 102 Avenue from 121 to 111 Street, the City says it chose to remove the westbound travel lane to fit a protected bike lane while retaining south-side parking. The November 2017 route map says the street had become one-way eastbound.
citations.establishes: The prior through-lane use, the City's stated reason for removing it, and the planned bike facility. The November 2017 map corroborates that the one-way change occurred: https://www.edmonton.ca/transportation/WestCentralBikeRoutes.pdf.

items.title: City to spend big bucks to remove bike lanes on 95th Avenue

citations.finding: In July 2015 council voted to remove the 2013 bike lanes on 95 Avenue (142–189 St) and 40 Avenue (106–119 St). Residents had complained about reduced parking and lanes of traffic. The removal cost about $500,000.
citations.establishes: That lane reductions in Jasper Place/West Edmonton and Whitemud were reversed and are not in the built-as-of-2026 set. Seen through the search index only.

items.title: Plans in Effect — District Plans
items.source_date: Page last updated 2026-08-27; original publication date not stated

citations.finding: The City's district-plan listing places Downtown and Glenora in Central and Garneau and Strathcona in Scona.
citations.establishes: The two district-plan areas assigned to the verified corridors.

items.title: Active Transportation Network Expansion — route and status table
items.source_date: Publication and last-updated dates not displayed; table contains 2026 status entries

citations.finding: The City's expansion table lists 95 Avenue from 149 to 156 Street as a proposed removal of one vehicle travel lane in each direction, but says implementation was deferred for further review; it also lists built routes without documenting prior lane use for every segment.
citations.establishes: The 95 Avenue proposal cannot be counted as built by 2026-09-23, and the consulted table is insufficient for a complete prior-use census.

items.title: Valley Line West Final Traffic Configuration; Valley Line West project update
items.source_date: Publication and last-updated dates not displayed; the linked project update describes summer 2026

citations.finding: For 102 Avenue east of 109 Street, the City attributes the permanent reduction from 107 to 102 Street to accommodation of the Valley Line LRT. Its project page says the 102 Avenue bike lanes were temporarily relocated to 103 Avenue in November 2025. These records do not identify a former through lane occupied by a bike lane on that named segment as of the freeze date.
citations.establishes: A competing explanation and a temporary route change; it does not establish that the named bike-lane conversion occurred. Relocation is reported at https://www.edmonton.ca/projects_plans/transit/valley-line-west.

items.title: 83 Avenue Protected Bike Lane Plan, April 2015; 83 Avenue Bike Route Project Fact Sheet, March 2017, p. 1

citations.finding: The April 2015 City design identifies 83 Avenue from 105 to 104 Street as previously two-way and specifies one-way eastbound traffic with a two-way cycle track. The March 2017 fact sheet schedules construction of the encompassing 99–106 Street section for 2017; the City's later network page calls the 83 Avenue protected route existing.
citations.establishes: A former westbound through movement and a bike lane on the converted block. Construction timing is documented at https://www.edmonton.ca/sites/default/files/public-files/documents/RoadsTraffic/2017_83_ave_bike_route_facts.pdf; later existing-route status at https://www.edmonton.ca/projects_plans/roads/active-transportation-network-improvements-project.

items.title: 2014/2015 Bike Route Plan — 102 Avenue Protected Bike Lane, April 2015

citations.finding: City fact sheet (April 2015), 102 Avenue protected bike lane. For 121 St to 112 St: a 2-way cycle track on the north side, next to an eastbound travel lane, and 'this section of 102 Avenue becomes a one-way street going eastbound only.'
citations.establishes: The City's design intent to turn two-way 102 Ave (121–112 St) into one-way with a cycle track. The direct fetch returned HTTP 502 on 2026-09-24; the content comes from the search index's extract of this document. It shows design intent, not what was built.

items.title: 132 Avenue Renewal: What We Heard Report, February 2022, pp. 11, 16; 132 Avenue Renewal project history

citations.finding: The 132 Avenue report describes a draft change to one driving lane each way, traffic-calming measures, and off-street bike paths. Construction was still proceeding on separate sections in 2026. The consulted record does not establish which completed segments replaced a former through lane with an on-street bike lane.
citations.establishes: Why the named 132 Avenue example cannot be counted from a draft design alone. The project history, including August 2026 construction status, is at https://www.edmonton.ca/transportation/on_your_streets/132-avenue-renewal.

items.title: 132 Avenue Renewal: What We Heard Report

citations.finding: The City's 132 Avenue renewal report describes a future bike route and renewal planning, but does not establish that a motor-vehicle through lane had been removed for it. The project therefore cannot be counted from this document under the brief's rule.
citations.establishes: The City identified 132 Avenue as a future bike route during renewal planning; it does not document prior through-lane use or a completed lane conversion.

items.title: West Central Bike Routes

citations.finding: A City map says more than 4.2 km of new protected bike lanes, shared roadways and paths had been installed in West Central Edmonton in 2017, including new bike routes on 127 Street and 102 Avenue. It corroborates installation of the 102 Avenue route but does not state prior motor-vehicle lane use.
citations.establishes: New bike routes, including the 102 Avenue route, were installed in West Central Edmonton in 2017.

items.title: Garneau Neighbourhood Renewal Final Design, updated April 2021, pp. 3, 5, 32

citations.finding: The Garneau final design specifies a protected on-street bike lane on 110 Street from 76 Avenue to Saskatchewan Drive and explicitly identifies removal of the southbound travel lane from 76 to 82 Avenue. A City mobility study reports Garneau renewal completed in 2023.
citations.establishes: The former southbound through lane and intended replacement on the qualifying segment. The May 2, 2025 mobility study reports completion of neighbourhood renewal: https://www.edmonton.ca/sites/default/files/public-files/assets/PDF/Priority-Growth-Areas-Mobility-Study-PartA.pdf.

items.title: Debate grows as Edmonton plans 23 km of new active transportation infrastructure for 2025

citations.finding: Delton: 'the city will convert 96 Street NW to allow one-way vehicle traffic and remove parking along one side of the street' to build ~830 m of protected bike lane. 132 Ave will 'turn the four-lane road into a narrower collector'.
citations.establishes: A lead that 96 St (Delton) was converted to one-way for a protected lane. The inventory shows 96 STREET NW one-way protected features dated 2024 (29) and 2025 (5).

items.title: Bike routes cancelled or put off despite council direction

citations.finding: Administration recommended re-evaluating 14 routes 'that would affect parking or vehicle lanes'. The committee received the report for information on 2026-08-26. Grovenor was cancelled; Terrace Heights (101 Ave) and 95 Avenue were deferred over traffic and parking impacts.
citations.establishes: That several lane- or parking-affecting routes were unbuilt, deferred or cancelled as of the as-of date, so they cannot add to A.

items.title: Bike Routes – On Street, ArcGIS layer 236 metadata
items.source_date: Layer publication and last-updated dates not displayed; metadata consulted 2026-09-24

citations.finding: The on-street GIS layer identifies route attributes and construction year but has no field identifying what occupied each segment before installation.
citations.establishes: Inventory geometry alone cannot establish R, C, or former through-lane use.

items.title: Bike Routes - On Street (MapServer layer 236) layer metadata and statistics

citations.finding: The on-street inventory has no prior-lane-use attribute. planning_change: null 2,877, Decommissioned 156, Upgraded 142. Of the 804 bike-lane-class features, planning_status is Constructed 136, Under Construction 24, Planned & Funded 29, null 615.
citations.establishes: That the counting instrument cannot supply R. It also cannot cleanly separate built from planned features, so a census of prior lane use needs a project-by-project document search.

items.title: Bike Routes - On Street (MapServer layer 236) query

citations.finding: Live inventory: 102 AVENUE NW has 27 'Protected Bike Lanes - Two Way' features, construction_year 2016 (15), 2017 (7), 2022 (5). Media report the Oliver lane opened in fall 2017, with 102 Ave going from two-way traffic to one lane between 111 and 121 streets.
citations.establishes: That a two-way protected lane exists on 102 Ave NW with 2016–2017 construction years. It does not record the prior lane use.

citations.finding: Live inventory: 132 AVENUE NW has 96 protected bike-lane features, construction_year 2023 (14), 2024 (22), 2025 (36), 2026 (18), 2027 (6).
citations.establishes: That most of the 132 Ave lanes were built between 2023 and 2025. The features dated 2026–2027 suggest the east section was not finished by the as-of date.

items.title: Community pushback forces City of Edmonton to change gears on bike lane plans

citations.finding: After protests, council directed an alternate 50 Street design that would 'maintain your lanes of traffic, maintain your parking' on about half the affected stretch. The original plan removed on-street parking, not a travel lane.
citations.establishes: That at least one prominent recent corridor was designed around parking, not travel-lane removal, and was not built as of the report.

items.title: Vehicles going wrong way on 102nd Avenue

citations.finding: Edmonton Journal, 2017-11-28, 'Vehicles going wrong way on 102nd Avenue'. Reports the Oliver lane's opening, with 102 Ave changing from two-way to one-way between 111 and 121 streets. I saw this through the search index only; the direct fetch returned 403.
citations.establishes: That the 102 Ave one-way conversion was reported as built by late 2017. It is a lead to the City record only.

items.title: Parking Change | Bike Lane

citations.finding: 100 Street, 76 Ave to 83 Ave: 'conversion of 100 Street to one-way northbound for vehicular traffic', with 'a two-way protected bike lane… from 83 Avenue to 80 Avenue'. Construction was expected spring to end of 2025. Taproot (2026-09-01) reports that 100 Street south of Whyte 'was built as part of the active transportation network expansion'.
citations.establishes: A community league's restatement, apparently of a City notice, that one through direction on 100 St was removed for a protected bike lane in the Scona district. It needs confirming against the City's project page.
citations.quote: conversion of 100 Street to one-way northbound for vehicular traffic

items.title: Edmonton's roadway renewal program looks beyond the automobile

citations.finding: The 132 Avenue collector renewal 'will narrow down the road's width from four to two lanes as a traffic-calming measure' between 127 Street and Fort Road, with 'a separated bike lane running in each direction'. Phase one broke ground in June 2023 next to Rosslyn and Lauderdale.
citations.establishes: That the 132 Ave cross-section went from four lanes to two with bike lanes. The stated reason is traffic calming on an 'overbuilt' collector (qualification 1). The City project page (https://www.edmonton.ca/transportation/on_your_streets/132-avenue-renewal) returned 502 and could not be checked.
citations.quote: narrow down the road's width from four to two lanes as a traffic-calming measure

items.title: How have Edmonton's Bike Lanes changed over time?

citations.finding: A cycling advocacy blog says 132 Ave infrastructure was added 'while maintaining enough capacity for the traffic volumes'.
citations.establishes: Only the advocate's position that capacity was adequate. It does not dispute the lane count, and it names no corridor where travel lanes were replaced.
